text:
Sasha: Heads-up — starting onboarding for athena-7B (quantized) to dedicated. We uploaded weights to gs://redwood-models/athena/v1/athena-7b-quant.pt and a small tokenizer JSON at gs://redwood-models/athena/v1/tokenizer.json. Quick ask: can someone sanity-check the chat template and BOS/EOS handling before I flip the config in staging?

Mike: I can take a look later today. Any failing infra checks so far?

Sasha: No infra failures. CI passed weight checksums. Problem is tokenization diffs in our eval harness — the tokenizer seems to emit an extra leading token in the chat template path, which breaks prefix caching. Repro:
```
prompt = "Human: What's the weather?\nAssistant:"
tokens = tokenizer.encode(prompt)
# expected: [101, 200, ...]
# actual:   [0, 101, 200, ...]  # unexpected leading 0 (BOS-like)
```

Tanvi: Ugh :grimacing: That leading 0 will shift KV cache indexing and cause one-token-off responses. Is 0 a reserved BOS in that tokenizer?

tokenizer-bot: Tokenizer metadata:
- bos_token: "<s>" (id: 0)
- eos_token: "</s>" (id: 2)
- pad_token: "<pad>" (id: 1)
- special_tokens_map: {"cls": "<cls>", "sep": "<sep>"}

Ryan: Did you test the chat-template vs raw prompt mode? Some tokenizers behave differently when you call encode_chat() vs encode(). Could be the shim used by the model-onboarding script.

Sasha: Good point. I ran both. encode_chat() returns no leading 0, encode() returns with 0 when the template contains a trailing newline. Likely a sentinel handling quirk. Example:
```
# chat template version
chat_template = ["<s>", "Human:", "{user}", "Assistant:"]
encode_chat(chat_template, user="What's up?") -> [101, 200, ...]

# raw prompt with newline
prompt = "Human: What's up?\nAssistant:\n"
encode(prompt) -> [0, 101, 200, ...]
```

Mike: That matches earlier weirdness we saw with one of the llama forks. For rollout safety, we should normalize tokens at the input layer (strip leading bos if present) and add a config flag so dedicated/staging can opt-in.

Tanvi: Agreed. Can we add a quick filter in the inference front-end? Pseudocode: 
```
def normalize_input_tokens(tok_ids):
    if tok_ids and tok_ids[0] == metadata.bos_id:
        return tok_ids[1:]
    return tok_ids
```
But be careful: some downstream evals expect preserved BOS. Need opt-in via model config: "strip_leading_bos": true/false.

Sasha: I'll add the flag to the model manifest (manifest.yaml) for athena. Draft: 
```
model: athena-7B
version: v1
weights: gs://redwood-models/athena/v1/athena-7b-quant.pt
tokenizer: gs://redwood-models/athena/v1/tokenizer.json
strip_leading_bos: true
chat_template: "Human: {input}\nAssistant:"
```
Putting it in staging first.

Ryan: Also check streaming semantics. If we strip BOS, make sure the runtime doesn't miscount tokens for byte-budgeting and for cost reports. We should subtract 1 token only if the flag was applied.

deploy-bot: deploy request: staging/athena/v1 manifest updated by Sasha. CI: unit + tokenizer normalization smoke passed. Canary: queued.

Mike: For the model-onboarding checklist, add these items: weights path validated, tokenizer metadata present, manifest flag set, eval prompt set including both chat_template and raw prompt cases, downstream integration test for prefix-cache. I'll open a tiny PR with that checklist.

Sasha: Thanks — PR would be great. Last small oddity: when using the chat template with sentinel replacement, some generated responses include an extra leading space because encode_chat kept an extra newline token. I can add a trimming pass on template rendering (strip trailing newlines) before encoding.

Tanvi: Please do that instead of normalizing tokens — trimming is lower risk. Only use strip_leading_bos for tokenizers that actually insert a BOS in raw encode() but not in encode_chat().

Sasha: Ok plan: 1) trim template newlines at render, 2) add model manifest flag strip_leading_bos=true for athena, 3) add normalize_input_tokens behind the flag in runtime, 4) run full eval harness including cache/regression tests. I'll ping when canary finishes.

Ryan: Ping me when canary is up — I'll watch logs for KV cache alignment errors and odd latency spikes.

Mike: I'll review the PR and the manifest changes this afternoon. Thanks for catching this early. :thumbsup:

Sasha: Awesome — appreciate the quick turn. Will post canary link + sample tokens once it's live. :eyes:
